lines.text: Some eighty islands in the South Pacific, settled by ocean voyagers and once ruled by two empires at once. This is the story of Vanuatu.
More than three thousand years ago, the Lapita people, makers of finely decorated pottery, sailed across open ocean and settled these islands.
In the sixteen hundreds a great chief, Roi Mata, ruled here. His home and his grave are now a World Heritage Site.
In the early twentieth century Britain and France agreed to rule the islands together, as the New Hebrides.
Walter Lini, a priest, would lead the islands to independence and become the first prime minister.
Jotham Napat, born in 1972, would become prime minister in 2025.
In 1980, as independence neared, a short rebellion broke out on Espiritu Santo, remembered as the Coconut War.
That same year the New Hebrides became the independent nation of Vanuatu.
In 2015 Cyclone Pam tore across the islands, wrecking homes and crops across much of the country.
And in December 2024 a strong earthquake struck the capital, Port Vila.
From Lapita canoes to a young nation, Vanuatu's people have weathered every storm.
